title: Strengthen the goal to A = ordinal for the converse of Schutte 13.6
intent: Prove the converse half of Schutte's characterisation of normal ordering functions by strengthening the goal to the convenient equality `A = ordinal` (from `segment A` and `Unbounded A`), which collapses `normal f B` to facts already at hand: `ordering_function f ordinal B` and the already-proved continuity lemma `Th_13_5_2`.
also_known_as: prove a more convenient statement first

parent.name: TH_13_6R
parent.statement:
Theorem TH_13_6R (A B : Ensemble Ord) (f : Ord -> Ord) :
  ordering_function f A B ->
  Closed B ->    Unbounded B ->   normal f B.

children.name: segment_unbounded
children.statement:
Theorem segment_unbounded : forall A:Ensemble Ord, segment A ->
                                        Unbounded A ->
                                        A = ordinal.
children.closed_by: apply Extensionality_Ensembles; split; the two inclusions close by `eauto with schutte` (the `intros; split` direction) and `destruct (H0 x) ... now apply H with x0` (the other direction).

children.name: SA1
children.note: Declared inside `Section ordering_function_unicity_1` with section variables `B A1 A2`, `f1 f2` and hypothesis `O1 : ordering_function f1 A1 B`, so outside the section it generalises to `forall B A1 f1, ordering_function f1 A1 B -> segment A1`; that is the exact shape the parent consumes with `eapply SA1; apply H0`.

children.name: ordering_unbounded_unbounded
children.statement:
Lemma ordering_unbounded_unbounded :
  forall A B f,  ordering_function f A B ->
                 (Unbounded B <-> Unbounded A).
children.closed_by: split; each direction applies `not_countable_unbounded` after asserting `Countable` via `countable_bij_fun`/`countable_bij_funR` with `Ordering_bijection`, then `countable_not_Unbounded`.

children.name: Th_13_5_2
children.statement: Lemma Th_13_5_2 : continuous f A B.
children.closed_by: split; the first conjunct by `red; case f_ord;tauto`, the second by `eapply A_closed` and `symmetry; apply f_sup_commutes`.
children.note: Declared inside `Section verso` (hypothesis `B_closed : Closed B`) inside `Section Th13_5` (variables `A B`, `f`, hypothesis `f_ord : ordering_function f A B`), so outside the section it generalises to `forall A B f, ordering_function f A B -> Closed B -> continuous f A B`; the parent applies it after `subst A` with `H0` and `H1`.

applicability.goal_shape: A goal `normal f B` (a conjunction `ordering_function f ordinal B /\ continuous f ordinal B`) under hypotheses `ordering_function f A B`, `Closed B`, `Unbounded B`, where `A` is a free set known only through those hypotheses and the goal's inconvenient form names the fixed object `ordinal`.
applicability.use_when: The goal is phrased over a fixed object (`ordinal`) while the hypotheses and the lemmas already proved are phrased over a free set `A`; replacing `A` by that object is what makes an already-proved lemma (stated over `A`) apply. Use when one strengthening equality makes the whole goal fall out of the hypotheses plus one reuse of a proved direction.
applicability.avoid_when: The strengthened equality (`A = ordinal`) needs a proof of its own that is no easier than the original goal; or the goal does not actually collapse to a known lemma after the substitution, so the strengthening does not line the goal up with existing facts.

consequences: The move replaces the two conjuncts of `normal f B` by one obligation `A = ordinal` plus two side conditions (`segment A`, `Unbounded A`). It is sound only because `segment A` + `Unbounded A` force `A = ordinal`; if `A` were merely a subset of `ordinal`, the `subst A` would not be valid. The single strengthened equality is then discharged by two further lemmas (`segment_unbounded` needs `SA1` and `ordering_unbounded_unbounded`), so the glue stays short but the real content lives in the children, and the payoff — the continuity conjunct — is a wholesale reuse of `Th_13_5_2`.
